messages.content: Write a self-contained fable of exactly 150 words about two parrots who disagree about sharing credit. Output no title or preamble. Include the final one-sentence moral in the 150-word total. Before responding, silently revise the draft until the entire response is between 140 and 170 words.

text:
The mango tree held two parrots who had painted the sky together, or so they claimed. Scarlet insisted the idea was hers alone; Emerald swore he had suggested it first. Their squabbling shook loose every ripe fruit.

A tortoise below collected the fallen mangoes and said nothing. Each day the parrots argued louder, and each day the tortoise grew fatter and happier.

One morning, a young sparrow landed between them. "Who taught you to paint the sky?" she asked. Both parrots fell silent, remembering old Kestrel, who had shown them the trick and never once mentioned his name.

Scarlet cleared her throat. "The idea was ours," she said. Emerald nodded slowly. "And the sky was Kestrel's gift."

They shared the next mango in silence, splitting it evenly, and invited the sparrow to eat with them.

Credit shared is credit doubled; credit hoarded is credit hollow.
